tier_reason: Upgraded: the independent gemmi shootout (project-gemmi/benchmarking-fft, code 1d.cpp/1d-r.cpp, GCC8 -O3, i7-5600U, single precision) shows meow_fft faster than KissFFT for C2C at n=256/384/480/512. The author's own README table (i7-4790, GCC 6.3.1 -O2 -g) has no public benchmark code, so on its own it would be C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: gemmi C2C (GCC8 -O3, i7-5600U): n=256 2120 vs KissFFT 2536 ns, n=384 4718 vs 4929, n=480 5745 vs 6030, n=512 4342 vs 6553 ns (~1.04-1.5x, derived from page data). R2C mixed: n=480 3591 vs 3140 ns (slower), n=512 2660 vs 2985 ns. Author README (i7-4790, GCC -O2 -g): N=1024 8.89 vs 13.12 us, N=8192 84.72 vs 119.38 us; N=64 slower (0.73 vs 0.58 us).
corrections.hardware: gemmi: Intel i7-5600U; author README: Intel i7-4790 @ 3.60GHz (also Core2 Duo P8400, ARMv7)
corrections.caveats: Scalar code only (no SIMD); author states it is slower than pffft, FFTW, muFFT, vDSP. Margin over KissFFT is small at many sizes; slower than KissFFT for N=64 (author) and R2C n=480 (gemmi). Author's FFTW3 column is flagged by the author as wrong (Hartley transform). Gemmi did not check accuracy. Repo has no benchmark code; gemmi plan setup times are similar to KissFFT.

notes: Tier upgraded C/B -> A based on gemmi's reproducible third-party shootout. Baseline KissFFT is correct; win is modest (up to ~1.5x).

tier_reason: README only says multi-D double precision performs 'fairly similar' to FFTW_MEASURE and single precision 'can be significantly faster', and that 1D is somewhat slower than FFTW; no numbers anywhere I found (README, web search).

corrections.claimed_speedup: No numbers. README: multi-D double precision 'fairly similar' to FFTW_MEASURE; single precision 'can be significantly faster'; 1D transforms 'somewhat slower than those provided by FFTW (if FFTW's plan generation overhead is ignored)'.
corrections.license: GPL-2.0-or-later; FFT component files (and their internal dependencies) are dual-licensed BSD-3-Clause
corrections.stars_or_usage: 32 stars on GitHub (a fork/mirror of gitlab.mpcdf.mpg.de/mtr/ducc, the primary repo); ducc0 on PyPI; README calls ducc.fft an evolution of pocketfft/pypocketfft used by NumPy and SciPy
corrections.caveats: No published numbers; 1D slower than FFTW per the author. GitHub repo is a mirror of the GitLab primary. ducc0.fft is the evolved successor of PocketFFT (same author, M. Reinecke); the PocketFFT C++ header branch still exists separately (used by SciPy). Fastest results need building from source with -march tuning (author: prebuilt wheels can be 2-3x slower).

notes: Possible duplicate: ducc0.fft is described by its author as an evolution of pocketfft/pypocketfft (same author); if PocketFFT C++ is already listed, consider folding ducc0.fft into it or keeping it as the newer variant. Kept at D because it is notable (successor of the NumPy/SciPy FFT).

First-party README graph (powers of 2, 16..16M, double): KFR 3.0.5-rc ~1.3-3x FFTW 3.3.8 FFTW_ESTIMATE MFlops (derived from page data, read from graph); similar to Intel IPP.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: README graph: clang 7.0.1 on Windows, AVX2; LVK paper: Clang (flags not stated)
corrections.hardware: Not stated (LVK paper says only 'Intel AMD64')
corrections.caveats: README graphs are old (KFR 3.0.5-rc) and compare against FFTW with FFTW_ESTIMATE, a weak planning mode, so they overstate the gap vs FFTW_MEASURE/PATIENT. LVK paper is graph-only with no CPU model. kfrlib/fft-benchmark harness is public but publishes no numbers. GPL or paid commercial license.
